notes: Snort 3 writes alert_json to stdout or to alert_json.txt, not to syslog, so have a forwarder send each line to the data collector with a syslog header, for example rsyslog imfile on alert_json.txt with the tag snort. alert_json fields are configurable. Use this fields line so each event carries what the NIDS schema holds: alert_json = { file = true, fields = 'seconds timestamp action msg class priority gid sid rev proto service dir src_addr src_port dst_addr dst_port pkt_num pkt_len pkt_gen iface vlan ttl tos ip_id tcp_flags tcp_seq tcp_ack tcp_win tcp_len icmp_type icmp_code' }. Lines on the default fields (src_ap, dst_ap and rule, with no message or classification) also normalize. The event time is seconds plus the microseconds in timestamp; without seconds the timestamp is read as UTC, so run Snort with -U. action is what Snort did with the packet: block, drop and reset set blocked, while would_drop and would_block are what an inline rule would have done on a passive sensor. ICMP over IPv6 gets protocol 58. alert_csv, alert_fast, alert_syslog, unified2 and Snort 2 output aren't covered. Samples are made up in the format alert_json writes, from the Snort 3 alert logging page and the logger's source. Passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (168 of 168 fields matched the emulator, in each of 2 runs). No built-in parser claimed these lines in 9 Run Tests.
